At line 20, we have `File file = new File(parentDirectory, dirs[i]);` - here `file` is created using `parentDirectory` (which was initialized from `outputDir`) and `dirs[i]`.

At line 24, we have `parentDirectory = file;` - this updates `parentDirectory` to point to the `file` object.

At line 22, `FileUtils.forceMkdir(file);` is called, where `file` is the File object created at line 20.

The key dependency is that `file` at line 20 (and subsequently at line 22) is constructed using `parentDirectory`, which was initialized from `outputDir` at line 14. Therefore, the value of `file` depends on the value of `outputDir` at line 14.
